title: Shadow
notes: This chunk assembles a dense, law-positive case that biblical shadow is protective shelter rather than disposable gloom, chaining tsel, wings, hand, tree-kingdoms, and overshadowing into a coherent rereading of Colossians 2. Scripture density and internal consistency are high; the Colossians turn lands cleanly once the evidence is stacked. Residual defects are almost entirely house-style: director cues (Hold the verdict, Read and notice, Now the equation, Now even) and multiple author-prose sentences that open with And, But, or That. No doctrine, quote, or factual errors require change; the listed fixes stay surgical and preserve voice and markup.

The chunk assembles the shadow-of-death texts with high density and ends on a sharp, law-positive close. Parallel columns and the light-behind-shadow claim land cleanly. The sole clear defect is residual presenter staging in the method paragraph, which breaks the no-director-cues rule and briefly shifts into meta-instruction. No grammar errors, sentence-open violations, or scripture-quote problems appear. The rest of the prose stays assertive and on-voice.

proposals.old: Hold the verdict on Colossians until the evidence is in; the verse will be waiting further down this road, and by then it will read as the opposite of a discharge.
proposals.new: The verdict on Colossians waits until the evidence is in; the verse stands further down this road, and by then it will read as the opposite of a discharge.
proposals.summary: Remove director cue Hold the verdict.
proposals.rationale: House style forbids Hold that and similar staging; rephrase asserts the same sequence without addressing the reader.

proposals.old: That is the habit to carry from this page: when the English wobbles between renderings, the wobble is a signpost — look beneath it.
proposals.new: The habit to carry from this page is this: when the English wobbles between renderings, the wobble is a signpost — look beneath it.
proposals.summary: Author prose must not open with That.
proposals.rationale: House rule bars That at the start of author sentences; the claim and cadence stay intact.

proposals.old: And Isaiah sets the definition in parallel columns — Scripture’s habit of defining a term by saying the thing twice:
proposals.new: Isaiah sets the definition in parallel columns — Scripture’s habit of defining a term by saying the thing twice:
proposals.rationale: Author prose never opens with And; the definition claim is unchanged.

proposals.old: And under the anointed king’s shadow Israel shall live among the heathen (Lamentations 4:20).
proposals.new: Under the anointed king’s shadow Israel shall live among the heathen (Lamentations 4:20).
proposals.rationale: House style forbids And at the start of author prose; the citation and claim remain exact.

proposals.old: Read the refuge verses again and notice what the shadow shields from: the heat.
proposals.new: The refuge verses name what the shadow shields from: the heat.
proposals.rationale: Director cues such as Read that and Notice that are banned; the assertion of content is direct and denser.
Author sentences may not open with And; the rhetorical question is preserved.

proposals.old: Now the equation closes, because we already know where the covering hangs.
proposals.new: The equation closes, because we already know where the covering hangs.
proposals.rationale: Now constructions are listed among forbidden director cues; the logical close remains.

proposals.old: But a shadow is not detached from its body; it is _attached_ to it.
proposals.new: A shadow is not detached from its body; it is _attached_ to it.
proposals.rationale: House style forbids But at the start of author prose; the attachment claim is unchanged.

proposals.old: Step back and take the lesson, because this chapter is a prime example of the whole method.
proposals.new: This chapter is a prime example of the whole method.
proposals.summary: Strip the director cue that stages the reader.
proposals.rationale: House style bans presenter cues such as Step back and take the lesson. The remaining clause keeps the author’s claim without meta-instruction.
